after.answer_quote: To avoid repeated losses for urgent or schedule-constrained residents, 10% of Open Pool blocks are reserved for urgent/essential use and recurring schedule windows, allocated by lottery among eligible applicants, and any resident who loses two consecutive Open Pool draws receives one priority ticket in the next draw.
after.conclusion: answered provisionally yes: the reserve and carryover are derived as access measures for urgent or schedule-constrained residents, subject to the stated falsifier that they must not crowd out newcomers or increase unused bookings
after.derivation: Read from AFTER ANSWER, this step adds two operative components to the Open Pool: (i) a bounded reserve of 10% of Open Pool blocks allocated by lottery among eligible urgent/essential and recurring-schedule applicants, and (ii) a consecutive-loss carryover granting one priority ticket in the next draw after two consecutive losses. The return states the rationale directly — to avoid repeated losses for urgent or schedule-constrained residents — and ties each component to exactly the access condition the question names: the reserve addresses urgent and schedule-constrained access, and the carryover addresses repeated lottery loss. The same step carries a public falsifier for the second half of the question: the additions would be contradicted if they failed to improve access for urgent or schedule-constrained residents without crowding out newcomers or increasing unused bookings. AFTER ANSWER also propagates the change: step 5, step 11 and the working-position claim all now name the bounded access reserve and consecutive-loss carryover, and the trial metrics add bounded access wait time, consecutive-loss rate, and urgent-reserve use. So the return supplies a reason that is substantive for this question rather than merely relabelling the bookkeeping string: it changes the Open Pool's eligibility and ticket structure in a way aimed at the exact access gap, and states the condition under which the change would fail.

before.answer_quote: The Open Pool is allocated by lottery: every resident gets one base ticket per block; a newcomer gets a one-time guaranteed first-use token and, for the first three bookings, one extra ticket; anyone who has not used the workshop in 90 days gets one extra ticket.
before.conclusion: undecided at BEFORE ANSWER: the Open Pool has no reserve or carryover component, so the question has no answering derivation in that state (not a substantive negative answer)
before.derivation: Read from BEFORE ANSWER, the Open Pool mechanism has exactly three ticket components: one base ticket per resident per block, a one-time newcomer first-use token with one extra ticket for the first three bookings, and one extra ticket for anyone unused for 90 days. No block is carved out ahead of the lottery for urgent or essential use, no recurring schedule window is protected, and no rule rewards a resident who has lost repeated draws. Therefore BEFORE ANSWER supplies no derivation that any bounded reserve or consecutive-loss carryover raises access for urgent or schedule-constrained residents, and it likewise supplies no derivation about whether such a reserve would crowd out newcomers or leave bookings unused, because the mechanism contains no such component to analyse. On the question as posed, BEFORE ANSWER has no operative step and leaves it undecided rather than answering it in the negative.

It wants newcomers to get a fair chance, experienced users to complete demanding projects, few unused bookings, and rules that residents can understand and challenge. The town does not know how demand or strategic booking will change once the rules are introduced. Design a workable allocation arrangement and explain why it should remain fair and useful as people respond to it.
